sections.h2: How owners usually sell in Buffalo Grove
sections.html:
Most Buffalo Grove owners list with an agent, because the housing market is built around mortgage-financed buyers and long-tenured owners. A direct sale to a cash buyer is the alternative when a house needs work or the closing date matters more than the top price.

The village adds one local step to every route. It sells its own real estate transfer stamps, in person only, and holds them back if water or other village debts are unpaid. Plan for the stamp early and it will not delay your closing.

  • Agent listing: more showings, more time, and the buyer's financing to wait on.
  • Owner sale: saves the commission, but you handle disclosures, the deed and the stamp visit.
  • Cash purchase: fewer contingencies and a closing date you set, usually at a lower price than a retail sale.

Lake Cook Road splits the village. The northern part, about three-quarters of Buffalo Grove, is in Vernon Township in Lake County, and the southern part is in Wheeling Township in Cook County. Anyone changing the property record with Cook or Lake County needs a village stamp.

The deed is recorded with the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division or with Lake County, depending on the parcel. Cook County Clerk's recordings hours run 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m. Property tax bills, exemptions and appeals follow the county, so find out which assessor and treasurer cover your parcel.

The village charges $3 per $1,000 for its transfer tax and will not issue a stamp while water, fines, fees or other debts to the village are outstanding. Stamps are sold only in person at Village Hall, 50 Raupp Boulevard.

Exempt examples include a seller that is a unit of government and a re-titling between an individual and a trust. All debts must still be paid before an exempt stamp is issued. Bring the stamp to closing so the county can record the new deed.

Water and sewer balances must be paid before the village issues a stamp, so settle the final bill ahead of closing. Rates as of January 2026 are $7.14 per 1,000 gallons for water and $1.77 per 1,000 gallons for sewer, a combined $8.91.

Houses on the Lake County side also pay a sanitary sewer pass-through fee of $5.26 per 1,000 gallons as of December 2025. That line shows on a Lake County bill and not on a Cook County neighbor's across Lake Cook Road.

The property check from the Finance Department is the fastest way to learn what you owe. Ask for the figure a few days before the closing date, then ask again if the date moves.

The median owner-occupied home value is $412,300, and 79.8 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. The 2020 count was 43,212 and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 42,812, down 0.9 percent. Median gross rent is $2,037, median household income is $129,395 for 2020 through 2024, and 88.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Population has been flat for years. Pricing against recent sales on your own street matters more than the village-wide median, which blends very different subdivisions. Most of the village was platted after the 1950s, so a buyer's inspector will compare your house with others of the same era.

sections.h2: State rules behind the village stamp
sections.html:
Illinois imposes its own transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, collected by the county recorder, and counties may add 25 cents per $500. Home rule municipalities such as Buffalo Grove can layer their own tax on top, which is why the village stamp exists.

Buyer and seller also complete the Illinois PTAX-203 transfer declaration, filed with the county where the property sits. Paper revenue stamps were scheduled for phase-out by December 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic stamps. The village's own stamp is still issued in person.

The split between counties also shows up in services. The Indian Trails Public Library District serves the Cook County part, and the Vernon Area Public Library District serves most of the Lake County part. Mention the right one in your listing so buyers know what to expect.

Buffalo Grove uses open space for flood control. Buffalo Creek forest preserve works as flood control, and the Buffalo Grove Golf Course is used as a floodplain. Buyers near those areas ask about basement dampness and drainage.

Gather sump pump service records and permits for any roof or foundation work. Those papers answer the questions before a buyer has to raise them.

sections.h2: Selling when the house needs work
sections.html:
A house with deferred repairs can still sell. Retail buyers who need a mortgage often ask for repairs or credits after their inspection, and a lender may balk at certain conditions. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so the sale depends less on what an appraisal or an inspection finds.

The trade-off is price. A cash offer usually lands below what a fully updated house could bring, so weigh the offer against the repair bill, the months of carrying costs while the house sits, and the date you need to close. The village steps are the same for each route, so they should not tip the choice either way.

A typical sequence runs like this. Order a property check from Finance and pay any balance. Schedule the final water reading. Fill out the village form with your buyer, and complete the PTAX-203 or MyDec form. Visit Village Hall with the deed or latest tax bill, the closing date and your forwarding address. Take the stamp to closing so the county can record the deed.

A cash buyer can run the same list in less time because no lender is waiting on paperwork. A listing buyer's lender may set its own deadlines, so ask the title company which dates are fixed.

faqs.q: How much is the Buffalo Grove transfer tax?
faqs.a: The village charges $3 per $1,000. You also give the closing date and a forwarding address when you buy the stamp.

faqs.q: Can I get a Buffalo Grove transfer stamp online?
faqs.a: No. Stamps are issued only in person at Village Hall, 50 Raupp Boulevard, after a property check with the Finance Department at 847-459-2500.

faqs.q: What blocks a stamp from being issued?
faqs.a: Delinquent water charges, outstanding fines or fees, or any other debt owed to the village. All debts must be paid before even an exempt stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Is Buffalo Grove in Cook County or Lake County?
faqs.a: Both. Lake Cook Road divides the village, with about three-quarters in Lake County's Vernon Township and the rest in Cook County's Wheeling Township. Your parcel determines where the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need a deed to get the stamp?
faqs.a: You need the deed or the most recent tax bill for the property. If you lack the deed, the Cook County Clerk or Lake County recording office can supply a copy.
